w: During Children's Day program a special tribute was paid to children who had participated in the Anti-addiction campaign. Children narrated their experiences, the 'Kafan' drama was enacted and Swamishri acknowledged their efforts and courage. More than 1750 children and 1500 parents had attended the assembly.

At 9.00 a.m. Swamishri departed from the Swaminarayan Mandir and went for darshan at the old Swaminarayan Mandir and shrine dedicated to Krishnaji Ada. Thereafter Swamishri travelled to Muli and had darshan of Thakorji at the Swaminarayan mandir built by Brahmanand Swami. At 12.25 p.m., Swamishri arrived in Surendranagar. In the evening assembly children presented a variety of programs.
Murti-pratishtha at New York Mandir

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of new murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Sita-Ram, Shankar-Parvati, Hanumanji, Ganapati and Guru Parampara at the BAPS Swaminarayan hari mandir in New York. Swamishri blessed 3000 devotees in the assembly.

The evening assembly was held at the Hofstra University Arena. During the assembly Thomas Gullata addressed the assembly, “Jai Swaminarayan, it is an honor for me to be able to be here in the presence of Swamiji and in the presence of all of you. Just being in this room in your presence and in the presence of a spiritual leader is an uplifting spiritual feeling. It’s impossible for anyone to be here without feeling the strength of spiritualism within. “But you know and I know it’s not the money that is important. It’s the spiritual values and spiritual strength and the family values that are important. I ask you to see the media reports, the television news and whenever there is a crime report you don’t see a young woman or a man of Indian descent that has violated the law, because of the understanding of spiritual values and family values and passing that along to the next generation. That is what will make the society grow and be what we hope in the future. Look around and understand that we live in the world of modern technology and modern medicine that cure the illness. But understanding in modern technology and medicine is the importance of spiritual values. Because when you grow older then you realise that human compassion, love and spiritual strength can create miracles that modern technology and modern medicines cannot. You all here are miracle workers. If you can reach out to others and neighbours and give them the compassion, love and spiritual wisdom you have, you too can create miracles in the lives of others.” In his blessings Swamishri explained about the pricelessness of the human birth and its ultimate objective of attaining moksha.

In New York today, Pramukh Swami Maharaj's morning puja had been arranged in the auditorium of the Mahavallabh Ganesh Mandir. Swamishri's car was moving towards it. At a bend, the driver, Jitubhai, turned the car to the left. Seeing this, Swamishri said, "Aren't we to go straight? Isn't that the way?"
Jitubhai said, "I have been told to come this way."
In fact the instruction was to bring the car to the back door of the auditorium, but since no one known was standing there, the car had to be brought by the very route Swamishri had pointed out.
Swamishri said, "It is good. Whatever happened, happened by God's will. We wanted to have darshan of the mandir, and that will happen now. This was God's wish."
Both Swamishri's outlook of taking everything positively and his devotion in having darshan of the deity in any mandir, according to Maharaj's command, could be seen together here.

At 7.00 pm a welcome assembly and volunteers’ assembly was held. Swamishri was honoured by the Mayor of Bhavnagar Shri Mehulbhai Vadodaria, Deputy Mayor Shri Jashvantsinh and Standing Committee Chairman Shri Tulsibhai. In conclusion Swamishri blessed the assembly, “I congratulate all the devotees for serving in the mandir project by disregarding all physical difficulties and discomforts. The summer heat is scorching but still you have served to please Shriji Maharaj, Gunatitanand Swami. The sadhus too have served immensely in the mandir project. You have engaged yourself in this project and attained a Ph.d. You have attained the Ph.d. You did not desire for material happiness, wealth or status but to please Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj”
At 10.20 am Swamishri departed from Gondal by car and arrived in Bhavnagar at 12.00 noon.
Honest and Humble Way

7 May 2006, Gondal “Should I go into politics?” a youth asked Swamishri. “What do you want to be?” Swamishri enquired. “A minister,” the youth replied confidently. “Not a minister, but a Prime Minister,” Swamishri added tellingly. “If you become a Prime Minister then it would be worth the while. Because when you become a minister, no one may respect you or ask of you later. So if you want to be a minister then be a Prime Minister.” “I want to be a Health Minister,” the youth trumpeted further. “First, study properly and then think about becoming a minister. But bear in mind if you are going to extort money then don’t go into politics. Never take another’s money (by corruption). Earn through your own sweat and toil, but never through deceptive or corruptive ways.” Swamishri agreed to the youth’s wish, but with the requisite of being honest. When the youth left, a satsangi youth, Jitu Patel, went to Swamishri and enthusiastically said, “I want to be a big, big sevak.” Jitu thought that Swamishri would be happy at the idea of becoming a sevak (humble servant). Swamishri perceived the resonance of ego in the youth’s words and answered, “There is no question of becoming ‘great’ at all. One should always become the smallest of sevaks. By saying a ‘great’ sevak, it reflects one’s ego.”
Pathway to Success
8 May 2006, Gondal

A youth came to seek Swamishri’s blessings because he was setting up a Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) production plant. Since it involved a lot of investment he said, “I have come to take your blessings. Whenever I lose hope, I wish your blessings shall be with me.” Swamishri replied, “God will be with you, if you do what I say.” Then Swamishri added, “Keep your satsang (faith) strong in life. Don’t allow any addictions and bad habits to enter in your life. And do the mala every day. Then God will be with you.” Swamishri prescribed personal spirituality, no bad habits and chanting God’s holy name for success in life.
Keys to Concentration
13 May 2006, Gondal

A child student asked Swamishri, “How can I concentrate?” “Firstly, don’t watch TV. Don’t read anything that is not related to your studies. Do your puja. Give up wandering or seeing that which is unnecessary and pointless. Study properly. If you travel and visit others all through your vacation then you will forget what you have learnt. So pay attention while reading, have restraint (saiyam), and control your eating habits. Do not listen to bad things. This will enable you to concentrate.”

At 9.35 am Swamishri departed from Nairobi by flight and landed at Entebbe airport near Kampala the capital of Uganda, at 10.55 am. Swamishri was welcomed by Bhikhubhai Patel (chairman), Ramjibhai Patel and other devotees. Swamishri was honoured as the state guest of Uganda by Mr. Ambrose, managing director of civil aviation. After a 45 minute drive Swamishri arrived at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Kampala. Swamishri was welcomed by the resounding ‘jais’ of devotees. Members of an African music and dramatic society welcomed Swamishri with a traditional African dance. After Thakorji’s darshan Swamishri sat briefly in the mandir hall and blessed the devotees. Thereafter Swamishri proceeded towards his living quarters.
Colonel Vijaykumar, chief secretary of the ashram of Yogacharya Ramdevji Maharaj, came today specially for darshan. Pramukh Swami Maharaj explained to him the glory of the holy place of Sarangpur.
He said, "I have had your darshan. It is my good fortune."
Swamishri said, "You had the wish and the feeling, so God made everything favourable."

Vijaybhai said, "We stayed one night in your satsang. I saw the life here, and today I wish to take refuge through your holy hands. I have done a great deal of worldly work. In the wars with Pakistan in '65 and '71 I carried out the responsibilities of a colonel, fought and served my country too. I have done everything. Now I want to reach God. How can we reach Him?"
Swamishri said, "Remember God every day. Read satsang books. Keep faith in God's strength and do five malas of Swaminarayan. Everything will be achieved."
Saying this much, as he wished, Swamishri gave him vartman and put a kanthi around his neck.

Various departments were at work in the preparations for the murti installation festival. Pramukh Swami Maharaj too kept himself informed of every detail of the work of these departments.

Today during the meal Swamishri was getting information about the plans of the water and electricity departments. Varniraj Swami spoke about the water distribution arrangements, and Yatiraj Swami and Paramvatsal Swami spoke about the electricity department.
At the end these sadhus said, "The water and electricity departments always work together, so that there are no differences of opinion."
Swamishri said, "That is good. Opinions may differ and views may differ, but whatever happens, understand each other, compromise and come to one view."

In the evening, after finishing, Pramukh Swami Maharaj said to Dharmacharan Swami, "Put a call through to Rajkot, I need Yogiswarup Swami." Dharmacharan Swami tried to call Yogiswarup Swami, but could not reach him, so Swamishri said, "Call Dharmakunvar Swami." When he came, Swamishri said, "There is Chunibhai Chaturvedi of Rajkot. He has grown old. He is an old devotee, so my wish is that he be called here for the festival, so that he can benefit from it. Arrange a car and arrange for him to stay right here in the mandir."
Dharmakunvar Swami said, "I will send a car to fetch him, and the accommodation will also be arranged."
Swamishri said, "We are just phoning Yogiswarup Swami, then we will tell you."
After a while Yogiswarup Swami's call came.
Swamishri said, "Where had you hidden yourself?"
"I had gone to bathe."

Laughing, Swamishri said, "Then that is right. If you hide in the bathroom, you certainly cannot be found!" Having said this, Swamishri spoke about Chunibhai Chaturvedi. So Yogiswarup Swami said, "I will tell him. When he hears that you remember him, he will be delighted. We will also arrange the car from here."
After a while Yogiswarup Swami phoned and said, "Hearing that you have called him, he was overjoyed."
During this conversation Narayanmuni Swami came into the room, so Swamishri told him too about Chunibhai.
Narayanmuni Swami said, "We had sent word to him, 'Come after the festival, so that you are not inconvenienced'; but since you have called him, it is fine."
Swamishri said, "He is an old devotee, a man of conviction, so I have called him so that he benefits from the festival. If he comes, keep a good person in his service."
Narayanmuni Swami said, "There is Janikaka of Mumbai. Earlier too, when Chunibhai had an accident, he served him. We will put him with him."

Thousands of devotees had come to the festival. Swamishri was as concerned for a devoted but ordinary devotee as he was for Chandrakantbhai Pujara, who, as the main host of the whole mandir construction, had done great financial seva. Even though Swamishri was busy every day with many arrangements in the preparations for the festival, in the midst of all this work Swamishri does not forget even an ordinary devotee.

Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the balcony to bless the devotees. Today, showering blessings, he said:
"Without money he is little Nathiyo, with money he is Nathalal;
Without glory he is a fool, with glory he is rich."

"If there is no understanding of glory in satsang, it cannot be called satsang at all. And the glory is real. It is not imagination. Maharaj is supreme, Gunatitanand Swami is Mul Akshar, and the great sadhus are real. And thousands of ekantik devotees have lived. These are not tall tales. Without glory, satsang cannot be understood; however much you struggle, it will not be understood. If glory comes from the heart, from the soul, the work is done. One who understands glory grows day by day in satsang. There is no other way to progress in satsang. Without glory, one may perform spiritual endeavours as big as Mount Meru, but they cannot equal an atom's worth of endeavour done with glory. Just as ten million mosquitoes cannot equal Garud.
Now the second thing: if devotees do not have love for one another, if there is contempt or hatred for anyone, then even if one performs countless endeavours, they are in vain.

Never keep the attitude 'I do not get along with so and so.' If we do not get along with someone, Shriji Maharaj will not get along with us. Glory is the life breath. Even if all our limbs are fine, what if the breath is choked? Know that it is the same without glory. Glory is the juice. Endeavours are the pulp. Glory and satsang are completely connected."
